questions.question: What is the physical meaning of real power in household appliances? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the physical meaning of real power in household appliances?
  • • Real power (P), measured in Watts (W), is the actual power dissipated by a load to
  • perform useful work. It is the component where energy is transformed into another
  • form.
  • • In appliances like irons or heaters, real power represents the heat generated. In
  • motors, it represents the mechanical torque produced. It differs from reactive power,
  • which merely cycles between the source and load.
  • • Formula : P=V I cosϕ, where cosϕ is the power factor.
  • (any two relevant points 5 marks. 2.5 marks mark for 1 point)

questions.question: Explain the working principles of following Disconnect switches a) knife switch b) Rotary switch c) isolator / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the working principles of following Disconnect switches: a) knife switch b)
  • Rotary switch c) isolator
  • • a) Knife Switch (2 Marks): A manual switch with a hinged metal blade. Closing the
  • blade into the slot completes the circuit.
  • • b) Rotary Switch (1.5 Marks): Operates by rotating a central spindle to select
  • between multiple circuit paths.
  • • c) Isolator (1.5 Marks): A mechanical device used to isolate a circuit for
  • maintenance, operated under "no-load" conditions.

questions.question: Describe the colour code of wires used in an extension board and explain the significance of each wire. / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the colour code of wires used in an extension board and explain significance.
  • • Phase/Live (2 Marks): Red or Brown. Carries current from source to appliance.
  • • Neutral (1.5 Marks): Black or Blue. Provides the return path to complete the circuit.
  • • Earth/Ground (1.5 Marks): Green or Yellow. Safety wire preventing shock by
  • grounding fault currents.
